paper_metadata.title: A Quantum Walk Model of Financial Options

summary: The paper proposes a discrete-time quantum walk option-pricing model using a Hadamard coin and 1‑D position grid, illustrated with 100-step walks and ensembles of 400 simulations. Using parameters such as 20% annual volatility, 2% risk‑free rate, and 6‑month maturity, the model generates option prices and implied-volatility surfaces that qualitatively resemble classical binomial/Black–Scholes results when combined with a supply–demand model. All results are obtained via classical simulations of the quantum-walk equations; no gate-based quantum hardware experiment is reported.

experiments.description: Discrete-time quantum walk model used to price European-style call options, compared against the classical binomial/Jarrow-Rudd model and then combined with a quantum supply-and-demand model to form a market price and implied-volatility surface.

algorithm.variant: discrete-time quantum walk with Hadamard coin; biased initial coin state; optional decoherent coin perturbation

hyperparameters.initial_state_biased: small bias toward higher prices; appendix uses start angle 50 degrees vs neutral 45 degrees
hyperparameters.decoherent_coin_form: Rn = (1/sqrt(2))[[1, e^{i zeta}],[e^{-i zeta}, -1]] with zeta ~ Normal(0, sigma_dec)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Balanced or slightly biased initial coin state; appendix sets start angle to 50 degrees (neutral 45 degrees)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: position basis states |x_j> represent discrete log-price grid points; coin state controls left/right movement
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute option value V_n = < (1/(1+r)^n) [exp(S_n)-K]_+ > from the final quantum-walk probability distribution over log prices
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Decoherence can be added to recover classical behavior; market price formed by combining buyer and seller propensities from quantum and classical prices

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing on a one-dimensional discrete log-price grid; market-price extension includes supply/demand and implied volatility/volume surfaces

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic option-pricing setup with initial price 1, strike varied, annualized volatility 20%, risk-free rate 2%

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Log-price interpretation of walk position; price increment adjusted to match target volatility; drift added for risk-free rate
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical/numerical computation of final probability distribution and option price; ensemble average over 400 simulations for decoherent case; comparison to classical binomial model and implied-volatility/volume surfaces

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical binomial/Jarrow-Rudd model; optimization routine for implied volatility; supply-and-demand model from Orrell (2020c,d)
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Set seller price to classical binomial price plus 10% margin; buyer price to quantum price plus 20% margin; add 0.001 floor; use 50-degree start angle
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute market compromise price, implied volatility by inverting classical binomial model, and transaction volume surface

classical_baselines.method_name: classical binomial model (used to invert implied volatility)

speedup_claims.factor: can be run directly on a quantum device; potential speed advantages for certain classes of problem
speedup_claims.conditions: if implemented on a quantum device; time step can be scaled to match final variance
speedup_claims.caveats: No concrete asymptotic or empirical speedup is quantified; the paper only states a potential advantage.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly stated; paper notes quantum walk can be run directly on a quantum device and suggests speed advantages for certain classes of problem
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly stated; classical binomial model implied

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified. The paper does not provide qubit counts, circuit depth, or a concrete gate-based implementation of the quantum walk required to achieve any runtime advantage.
limiting_factors: No gate-based circuit implementation of the quantum walk is provided

notes: The paper describes a quantum walk model and states it can be implemented directly on a quantum computer, but it does not specify a concrete gate-based hardware platform, qubit count, circuit depth, shot count, or transpilation details.
The 'decoherence' case is a model parameterization within the quantum-walk simulation, not a separate hardware noise study.
The paper only states that the quantum-walk model 'can be implemented directly on a quantum computer' and may offer speed advantages for certain classes of problem (Section 5).
No empirical or theoretical runtime comparison demonstrating advantage is presented.
